tips.comment: Law Degree has been knocking on the door since entering handicaps and went down by just a neck at Redcar last time. He’s consistent, the drop to 7f should be fine, and with a top trainer at Beverley, he looks ready to get his head in front.
Not beaten far in 2 runs this year. Was closing all the way to the line last time out, and this extra 1/2 furlong can help.
Beltsdaay won last time out before a break and will need to go well fresh. But under a fairly low weight, he has the experience to follow up that win.

Berkshire Smudge is still without a win but has a chance to shed that maiden tag in a race that lacks any real quality. He takes a drop in class, and the return to turf might suit as his last two runs were on the AW.

Seed Investor didn’t get the clearest run at Southwell last time but still ran with credit, and his overall profile is solid. Cheekpieces go on for the first time, conditions look spot on, and while he may just need this after the break, he’s got a definite chance if tuned up.
Sovereign Class looked class when finishing 2nd last time out. Although this looks a tough affair, it has a weight advantage and shouldn't worry too much about the draw. 4 places at 10s looks value.
Just a lightly raced maiden who has performed well on turf, so should welcome a return back to turf tomorrow. He has a chance if he can take advantage of the dropped mark.

Blueandtangerine relevant recent runs have been in 7.25k avg class, whereas the avg of the rest of the runners is 7.47k (Going up in class (on average) today). Ranking the 34 relevant recent run class ratings of the entire field shows Blueandtangerine as running in the 2nd, 21st, 12th, and 12th most difficult recent races. Ranking the 34 relevant recent form ratings of the entire field shows Blueandtangerine as having the 9th, 1st, 26th, and 13th best ratings. Bet. (KEY - Best Max Rating, Beverley Flat.) (7½f (7f96y) Hurn Handicap (Class 5) (3yo 0-70)).'
Placed three times last year, slight drop in rating from last time out. Highest average speed out of all horses running in this race.

SUZETTE won a nursery handicap from this mark at Carlisle in August, before being unsuccessfully tried at a higher grade at Ayr and York. First run as a 3yo was after a lengthy break so is forgiven and she could fare better now back to this grade and weight. Stable not in bad form and tend to do better with the sprinters.

Crown's Lady relevant recent runs have been in 4k avg class, whereas the avg of the rest of the runners is 3.89k (Dropping in class (on average) today). Ranking the 24 relevant recent run class ratings of the entire field shows Crown's Lady as running in the 9th, 1st, and 14th most difficult recent races. Ranking the 24 relevant recent form ratings of the entire field shows Crown's Lady as having the 2nd, 1st, and 2nd best ratings. 1pt Bet. (KEY - Min Rating > All Others Max RatingsAvg Rating > All Others Max Ratings, 3 of Top 5 Ratings, 3 of Top 3 Ratings, Best Avg Rating, Beverley Flat.) (1m½f (1m100y) Racing Again Next Thursday Fillies' Handicap (Class 5) (4yo+ 0-68)).

Mick Easterby has a decent hand here and this one especially could start off well this season off her lowest mark. She has form at 1m in a class 2 and back in calmer waters could be ready to fire from 9 months off. Not sure where Jo Mason is but Tom Eaves might get a better tune, you never know.
Casilli is a confirmed performer at both this course and distance and on this ground. Sam James is a good jockey booking for the yard and will go well here.

Mystical Maria didn’t quite see it out over 11f last time, so the drop back in trip should suit much better. She’s shown ability in shorter races and if settling into a good rhythm, she’s got a fair chance of getting involved here.

Coming bang into form with a couple of recent fourths, and the stiff uphill finish at Beverley will definitely help as the horse keeps staying on in its races on flatter tracks. Still just three pounds above its last winning mark, this represents a really good chance for another victory.
Only won once in 26 attempts, but has gone very close 2 and 3 runs back from marks of 50 and 52. Comes here off 51, so may nick a place with 4 being on offer.

Since her last win in 2024, she has participated in 14 races. 8 days ago, she secured a respectable 8th place out of 13 in a handicap at Southwell, demonstrating a solid performance in the final stretch. As she steps onto turf for the first time, she may not have the accolades of others, but there's a strong chance for her to make considerable progress. At odds of 25/1, she offers great value for an each-way bet.
Achieved 3 wins from 18 runs last year but is also a 5-time course winner. This outing will be a bit tricky going up in class, but has won 3 of her last 4 runs, so has bags of ability.
A tip in itself that Cobden has come here instead of Cheltenham. Nicholls has a few runners, and this Kap Boy looks like one of his best chances. Small win.
Could be an interesting runner from the Henderson yard, who showed promise on debut but did not really build on that last time out. Give this one another chance now back in company.
Promising third in a soft-ground Exeter bumper, with the form franked since. Makes hurdles debut in a modest contest and looks a likely improver for a yard in good form.

Ran his best race yet at Exeter last time when back down at 17f having made his hurdles debut over 26f. That last run saw him taking 4th spot late on and given his likely SP looks a fair each way prospect.

This is a relatively small field and has the scope for an upset. I can see the market leader, but there is value here for Silver Sam, who finished 6th on debut and would have learnt a lot from the run. Can outrun his odds here and place.
Well beaten in all starts to date, but steps up in trip and returns to testing ground. Could show more with experience and conditions to suit if taking a forward role.

Star Walking looked to appreciate three miles last time when held up at Doncaster but did not get a clear run through when only 4th in a Listed novice hurdle. Back to a handicap she should do much better than her only previous handicap at Fakenham when an underperforming well beaten favourite and Harry Cobden is booked to ride.
Returned from a long layoff with a fourth at Sandown in a better race than this. Followed that with an improved effort at Ludlow and should come on again for that.
Lightly raced for her age and looked revitalised when scoring over this trip at Ludlow. Only up 4 lb and remains unexposed at 3m, every chance if backing it up.

Ran right up to form, only beaten 6L when fourth in a mares' novice hurdle Grade 2 over 2m 5f at Newbury. Now down in grade but up in trip. If stamina holds out, the trainer is confident it will, then solid each way NAP for me today.
8-year-old mare has been running well in chases and finished second in her last two chase races. Handicapped fairly, she has serious claims in this now reverting back to hurdles.

Had a recent run over hurdles and now returns to chasing. Has run well prior to that hurdles run over fences. Just needs to find that little extra, and it might be the drop back in trip will see that happen.
Yet to win, but has run some solid races in this grade. Latest 2nd is good enough form for this moderate race with the 4th and 5th placed since.
Is coming here after a small break, and past runs prove this is a positive. CD winner as well. Looks to be on a lenient mark.
Lightly raced hurdler who looked promising before falling on chase debut when hampered. Has scope to improve over fences with that experience behind him if jumping holds up this time.

PILSDON PEN still not entirely exposed as a chaser should give a good account with the yard having enjoyed a fruitful spring. This eight year old showed up well enough on his recent reappearance following a huge absence and second spin back could be the right time to have him on side.

Not the greatest of runs on both latest runs and is surely better than them. In fact, it might just be a case of going the wrong way. Beaten on two right-handed tracks and now returns to a left-hand venue. Might see this Henderson runner regain winning ways.

The Harry Derham-trained Ninth Loch won nicely at Chepstow 11 days ago, where he settled much better. I don’t think he had a particularly hard race, and he should have no problems with the ground. He can go very close again tonight.

The model I run has simulated this race and has El Granjero coming in first ahead of Kado De Joie in second and West to the Bridge in third. El Granjero has the joint second highest RPr of the field and steps out with a reasonable weight to carry for the 2m 4f trip. Ned Fox on board has 3 lbs claiming, which helps lower the ask and just tilts the race to favor.
Eaton Anne won a couple of handicaps during the winter, disappointing last time out but worth another chance at these big odds.

Well thought of by Skelton, and though his future will be over fences, he has a great chance from this mark. He won last October, and the 2nd won his next 2 races. That form alone makes his mark of 124 today look very generous, and he is down in grade from his last 2 runs.
First run since May 2023, so could understandably be rusty. But has won here before, the last run out, and four wins in a short career so far across hurdles and flat.
This selection is my personal preference. Anything I bet on looks to have a chance based on statistics and past results or recent form. Good luck if you follow and gamble responsibly.
Has been freshened up since disappointing last time, but he had won his 2 runs prior to last time, and he should go close to winning this.

Another Lord was run out of it over course and distance ten days ago by Airtothethrone but could get his revenge on seven pounds better terms, not including seven-pound claimer Lewis Saunders taking over on Airtothethrone. Yet to win this season, he has been 2nd three times.
Won over course and distance last time, and he goes up 7lb. But connections put up a 7lb claimer, which negates the 7lb. If he handles the softer ground, he will go close to following up.

Try The Money has run well at this track a few times without winning and was closest to doing so when staying on 3rd over hurdles here - 2m4f good to soft last April. Has been chasing since and learning this game, proving he has the stamina for 3m in the process. On a low mark and looks like he still has more to offer. Big chance if putting it all in today.

Came 3/8 beaten 2.25 lengths to another of today's runners Bampton Star in a similar class chase over 3 miles @ Exeter. Goes off same mark here, is a C,D winner, under used jockey up who rides some nice winners for this stable and very good trainer has done extremely well @ this course last 5 seasons, making current 11/1 very good Ew value here.
This selection is my personal preference. Anything I bet on looks to have a chance based on statistics and past results or recent form. Good luck if you follow and gamble responsibly.

The model I run has Just Aidan to win this one, coming in ahead of Highbury Hill in second and Rodney in third. This result has been driven by Just Aidan having the second highest RPR of the 12 runners, but a kind OR meaning slightly less weight to carry than the rest of the market leaders.

L’Empire Vert comes into this off a solid second-place finish and carries top weight, a sign of handicapping respect. At just five years old, he still has room to improve. Trainer Sheila Lewis has him in good shape, and if he reproduces his latest run and settles into the pace, he’s a strong contender here.

KYLENOE DANCER is interesting making her debut at the foot of the weights for a high-profile trainer combination. It also catches the eye that ace jockey Harry Cobden comes to Ffos Las for a late ride on a Wednesday evening. Maybe in her time spent absent this mature mare has improved considerably and this is a weak handicap hurdle which will not take much winning.

Should come on for solid C/D run LTO in a class 4 which was their first in over 5 months. Drops to a class 5 here off 2lb lower mark, is a C/D winner, good conditional up claiming 5lb and in hands of an upcoming trainer, ( does run another one in the race), making current 10/1 the Ew play here.
Showed little in three novice runs but goes handicapping for a yard that does well in this sphere. Could take a big step forward if finding improvement off a low mark.

Valedictory showed loads of promise on debut when a close third at Doncaster and looked to have plenty left in the tank. Steps up in trip which should suit, and with a top jockey and leading yard behind him, he’s the one they all have to beat.
Won on debut under a hands and heels ride when last seen. Form franked and comes here with expected improvement now he is upped in trip.
Encouraging debut when third at Kempton, staying on nicely without pressure. Bred to improve over this longer trip and now fitted with a tongue tie, big run looks likely.

This one is quite an expensive purchase, making his debut for a good yard with Oisin Murphy riding. He is a Frankel colt, and his progeny usually go well first time up, often winning. He is related to several winners, so he could be the one to beat if the trip suits on debut.

Chess Dad made an impressive winning debut just over 12 weeks ago at Newcastle over a mile and was not stopping that day, so the extra two furlongs shouldn't be an issue. Rossa Ryan is an interesting jockey booking for the yard. Surely there is further improvement, and he should be thereabouts to stay unbeaten in a race where a market check for newcomers to their expectations. Race fitness advantage is a major plus.

Made an encouraging debut on the all-weather for a shrewd trainer when running green before getting the hang of things late, staying on nicely for fourth. Looks sure to be suited by this step up in trip and a bigger track to run on to utilize what looks a big stride. A tougher race but looks overpriced here. Each-way Nap at 20/1.

A Dubawi progeny won on debut earlier in race two, and he is represented by Lemurian, who will definitely go better here on the turf despite his poor debut run, as Dubawi progeny generally perform at their best on the grass.

Stardrop was not bad after a duff start on debut last month when fourth of nine and seemed to be getting the hang of things on the run-in. So, worth another shot now second up, but with Harry Davies this time EW.

Fifty Nifty looked a smart prospect last year, winning both starts including a smooth handicap success off 87 on the July Course. He’s up 6lb and returns from a break, but remains unexposed and likely has more to come.
Has solid form last year and could well go on from that. With the stable in great form, I would expect this Balding horse to go well.

Making his debut with blinkers, he won a 7f maiden at Chelmsford on the all-weather in October, marking his sixth and final start for the Gosden team. After being sold for 28,000gns, he ran poorly in November on his first outing for his new stable, finishing last in a handicap while still wearing blinkers. However, when switched to a hood for a 14-runner handicap at Doncaster (7f, good) 17 days ago, he showed improved form, producing a strong late run to win at 25-1. The 3lb rise for this victory seems fair, but he returns to blinkers for this outing.

You’re only getting 2 places here but FAHRENHEIT SEVEN can be chanced at 7/1. Fifty Nifty is probably the right fav but he’s a T Clover runner in spring on reappearance so I’ve got to oppose, meanwhile Miss Information carries a poor FlatStats rating and is unlikely to offer much value. While Ten Pounds is 3/5 over this trip H Charlton runners over 7f are wildly overbet (9% SR, A/E 0.47) so his charge is probably short enough and Jumby’s best days are probably behind him (hasn’t won since June 2023). I can’t make a case for the remaining couple but FS appeals given he’s race fit with a 1.25l 3rd of 7 at Newcastle in March and neck success at Pontefract 8 days ago. Connections are upping him a couple of furlongs but he’s unexposed at this trip with just a 1.25l 3rd of 9 at Doncaster to his record and his previous runs suggest he’ll relish the extra distance. A Farragher’s 18% SR (A/E 1.61) on Wednesdays boosts claims further.
Very likely to throw the spanner in the works here, now dropping down in class and four pounds better than when third of eight last September. Could have been my NAP.

The outsider of the field at 11/1. Would not be surprised to see him being shorter come post time. The seven-year-old has form over seven furlongs, and the gelding could be producing a telling run with Jason Watson, who won on him here last June. Admittedly on good to firm ground, he has also won on soft at Sandown. Looks like he can adapt accordingly to conditions. David O'Meara's only runner at the meeting today, waiting until the lucky last could be a fruitful one.

The 7yo wasn’t great in the second half of last year but returns from a 6 month break on an attractive mark. He ran a few nice races last spring, winning off a 6lb higher mark and going close on his next start off a 10lb higher mark. The yard is going well and he can return in better shape.

A 5-time career winner up to 2m1f, twice in bumpers and 3 times in hurdles, the last one coming at Huntingdon last November. Yet to hit form in 3 starts this year but ran fairly well in the County Hurdle at the Cheltenham Festival last month when staying on 11th of 16, beaten around 8 lengths. Good chance here now down in class.
This looks like a good bet to me. He has had some decent form franked this season and is finally showing signs of fulfilling early promise. Can get a win here with ground and conditions to suit.
Placed in a better race than this last time, so has a very good each-way chance here if handling this better ground. Has one of the better conditionals on top in this amateur/conditionals race.
Continuance is on a hat trick here. Although this is a tougher contest than his previous two, he still looks well treated, and the handicapper hasn't quite caught up with him yet.
Casa No Mento won last time out (as did others), but that win looks very good on paper. It is well treated here and can go in again for a trainer who knows how to get a Cheltenham winner.

He has to put behind him a poor run last time out when he tried chasing, which he didn't seem to enjoy. He's run a couple of decent races here at Cheltenham. Still lightly raced, I'll take a chance he can make the frame at least here.

Big Boy Bobby has returned from a long break with 2 eye catching runs - beaten 1 length by Ooh Betty (same jockey takes the ride) who was only beaten half a length in the Scottish Champion Hurdle and then seen off when runner up to a well backed and promising handicap debutant at Newcastle. Only win over obstacles was on good ground and a winner on good to firm on the flat - so the drier the ground the better for this selection. Alan King horses are in good nick (won the Champion Chase at Ayr) and a further 3 runner up efforts from last 8 runs. NAP

Liverpool Knight was second and third in the last two runs. Although climbing up the weights without winning, he has a very handy 5 lbs claimer onboard today, which could make the difference with the trainer Fergal O'Brien having won this last year. EW 5P.

When Mary stays on her feet, she is very consistent and is worth an each-way value selection here. She is in receipt of weight from all rivals and now back over hurdles could well outrun her price. If they run to their last run over hurdles at Newbury in November, she could go close.

Champs Elysees sired a mare who is trained by Nicky Henderson, who has Freddie Gordon in the plate. Freddie rode East India Express, who won with authority earlier. With Freddie riding with confidence, he can give Arclight the vibes to hurdle well here and be in the mix at the finish. Coming here fresh, she can express herself.
Has form @ this class 3 level and has dropped to a attractive mark of 114 here. Under used jockey up and in hands of a shrewd trainer, making current 18/1 decent Ew value in the race.

I'm going to take a chance on Ashington, who I believe is overpriced at 22/1. He put in a solid performance last time out, finishing 5th of 16 at Kelso, and had previously scored a win off a mark of 115. With Tom Midgley taking 3lb off, Ashington effectively returns to that same winning mark for this upcoming race at Cheltenham. While his form has been a bit inconsistent, I think the good ground will play to his strengths. Given his previous performances and current mark, he looks capable of outrunning his odds. At this price, I'm happy to have an each-way bet, as the value is certainly there.

This 10 year old, a 2 time winner of handicap hurdles during the 2020/21 season, has achieved 4 victories since then, including a recent win over fences at Ayr in January. He has delivered commendable performances in his recent outings, and with an experienced jockey holding a 7lb claim, he stands a good chance of surpassing his 4th place result in the 2023 race. Betting each-way at 25/1 offers excellent value.
Well held since last summer's big win at Market Rasen, but went well in this race last year and returns fresh. Could outrun big odds if back near his best.

Plenty in with chances in this 16-runner 21f Class 3 handicap hurdle for Conditionals/Amateurs jockeys. The Anthony Charlton-trained 8-year-old Getaway gelding Way Out was initially a 90k purchase but hasn't really lived up to expectations after winning a Novice Hurdle by 10 lengths over 2m2 1/2f good/soft back in September 2023. This is only his second start for new trainer AC, and straight away he has dropped him down in trip to 17f from 21f. I like this move if making plenty of use of him as he will obviously stay the trip. He will love the ground, has course form, only 3lb above last winning mark, but Luke Scott takes off his 3lbs claim, could out-run his odds and nick a place.

Sent off favourite for the Grade 1 Juvenile Hurdle at the DRF, Saint Lucie bombed out and finished last of the 8 runners. She was put into the Grade 1 Triumph off the back of that run and finished mid-division, never really in the race. Into handicap company today from a mark of 131, I'd be shocked if she wasn't better than that if coming on for her runs in the spring festivals. No surprise to see her ridden more prominently down in grade as she was when winning her maiden by 11L, comfortably beating two rivals now rated 122. She's had just the four career starts and is entitled to be improving at a rate. She can outclass her rivals, and I'd be surprised to see her anywhere near 11/4 near the off.

A progressive 7yo, winning 4 of 7 hurdles races in the last 12 months, plus a couple of near misses. Loves the quicker ground and looked good when winning last month after coming off a 4 month break and after a wind-op. Winning with the minimum of fuss, sprinting through the line over the 3m trip, winning by 3L. More to come from her and still on a handy looking mark.

Sainte Tartare is a 7-year-old daughter of Saint des Saints ex Nuance Tartare. She runs here off a mark of 125 in this 2m4f Mares Listed Novice Hurdle. She'll be ridden by D Mullins for his uncle WP Mullins, and she wears a hood. Last time out, she won her 2m mares maiden hurdle at 1/3f by 21 lengths at Limerick in January. The stable is in top form at the moment. I think she can gain some Black Type here. I make her my Nap of the day.

The 7yo is capable on his day, win or placed in 15 races. Loves the better ground and ran two decent races last summer in a couple of quality class 2 handicap races. Around 10lb better off now with a capable 3lb apprentice in the saddle for this class 4 handicap. Hopefully a 5 month break will light a spark on his return.

The 7yo has been hit or miss in his career, however, he was a good runner-up on the AW four weeks ago after coming off a 7 month break and looks in good shape - something to build on. He was a runner-up in a class 2 handicap last spring off a 6lb higher mark, and is now running in a class 4 handicap.

Lightly raced gelding who was last seen at Wolverhampton over the 7 furlong trip 12 days ago where finishing 4th/11 and that run was full of a lot more promise than the bare result is suggesting as he wasn't ideally placed on the occasion and came extremely wide into the home straight losing a lot of ground in the process of that bend however he kept on from the rear of the field with real promise and hit the line very strongly and full of running now that was a pretty strong performance under those circumstances and he was also returning from a 253 day break on the occasion so he is most certainly entitled to strip fitter steps up in trip tackling the full 1 mile trip for the first time that being a positive move by his connections as this trip can unlock a whole new level of improvement and now in a fitter state expect to see this good looking chestnut trained by Richard Fahey thundering home with jockey Billy Garrity taking the ride current operating mark of 64 is well within range and he must enter calculations here

Up 6 lbs for Trial Day win when overcoming a wide trip to win fairly comfortably. Trainer wasn't sure he'd like Lingfield, but he'd won here at Newcastle the time before, so today's track is not a worry. Only 3 years old, plenty of improvement is possible to come. May defy the rise bearing in mind the Trials win wouldn't have suited. Sired by Too Darn Hot from a Lope De Vega mare, he's bred to progress.

Simply can't have that. He's an 11/1 shot here. Won at this level already when beating Rebels Gamble by 1.75L, who since went on to win a Listed race by 1.75L from Rajeko, which stacks up well. Disappointing the next time in Class 4 Southwell Handicap when beaten 0.5L at 5/6. Just seemed to not pick up when needed and was nothing like his previous performance. Maybe uncomfortable under heavy weight; however, he's been dropped 1lb as a result and can go well here.

Fairly consistent over 6f around this - Listed level. 2 Class 2 and Listed win to start the season before dropping to 5f to finish 0.5L 2nd to Clarendon House. Not the world's best form that run, however, it was encouraging over a suboptimal trip. Followed that up 2.25L 3rd behind Spycatcher on officially Good To Soft. However, with the winner being a Soft ground performer, I think it's safe to assume the ground was on the softer side. Regardless, he never looked overly comfortable throughout, so he has excuses. Would imagine this has been the plan for some time and has every chance to get it done if running to his best.

Ran a good race to beat Old Harrovian over 1m3f, then followed it up with an impressive win of 3.25L in a class 2 handicap off 2nd top weight. Took a second to get going there, but once in top gear, he put it to bed very quickly. Slight concern the drop to 1m2f might not be optimal. However, he is very lightly raced for a 6yo and could still progress to a graded performer.

Top weight is always a concern, but the manner in which he won last time out when pulling clear by 5 lengths in the trial was very impressive. Up 8 lbs as a result; however, I'm pretty sure he had more than 8 lbs in hand with that win. Course and distance winner. Connections talked about the Dubai Gold Cup, and they're pretty confident that he's a Cup horse. Should be 6/4 in my opinion.
